definition: DRP is named in the archive only as a comparison point for other efficiency methods, and the two sources place it slightly differently. The efficient-R1 survey files it under model consolidation, as a distillation approach alongside LiteCoT/DAR and TwT that compresses a large teacher's reasoning into a student. FROST treats it as the supervised-fine-tuning representative among efficiency baselines — contrasted with prompting (TALE) and RL (SelfBudgeter, ThinkLess) — and evaluates against it on GSM8K, MATH500, AIME24 and Minerva with Phi-4-Reasoning and GPT-OSS-20B. Neither source expands the acronym or states the method, so nothing here defines it beyond 'a training-based chain-of-thought shortening method'.

evidence.note: A survey that organizes methods for making R1-style large reasoning models reason efficiently (i.e., avoid overthinking) into two axes: single-model optimization and multi-model collaboration.
evidence.title: Don't Overthink It: A Survey of Efficient R1-style Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: FROST uses attention weights to identify and prune sentence-level 'reasoning outliers' from a reasoning model's chain of thought, reporting an average 69.68% token reduction and 26.70% accuracy gain over the base model on four maths benchmarks.
evidence.title: FROST: Filtering Reasoning Outliers with Attention for Efficient Reasoning

name: DRP
